question: Does the public repository record for Orozco and Dayao (1996) provide fish data or a traceable station-level fish result for Estero Aviles?

source.title: The physio-chemical analysis and fish study of Estero Aviles
source.citation: Orozco, G. P., & Dayao, L. (1996). CHS Research Monitor, 19(1), 1–11.
source.repositoryFinding: The DLSU Animo Repository identifies an 11-page 1996 article and provides an abstract. Its Upload File field says wf_no and the page states that the document is currently unavailable there.
source.alternateAccessSearch: A bounded exact-title search returned the same DLSU record and secondary citation mentions, but no alternate full text. This is not an exhaustive archive search.

abstractFindings.reportedSampling: Water samples are described for four stations across three morning and three afternoon trials.
abstractFindings.fishInformation: The title and first sentence call the work a fish study/survey, but the accessible abstract provides no scientific fish names, fish sampling method, catch counts, specimen identifiers, or fish-specific station assignments.

evidenceDecision.decision: Add the repository record as an Estero Aviles historical source and waterbody-scope lead; hold all fish evidence until the underlying article or another primary source supplies it.

nonClaims: No fish taxa in the abstract does not mean no fish were present or caught in the study.
The four water-quality station names are not coordinates and do not establish a verified shoreline or reach geometry.
The abstract does not establish present-day water quality, fish presence, catchability, fishing access, or legal harvest conditions.
The record does not provide enough information to count fish captures, compare species composition, or link any species to a station.

rightsReview.finding: No item-specific open license or permission to redistribute the article was identified on the repository record.
rightsReview.handling: No full text, article table, image, or underlying data were accessed or retained.

nextActions: If an authorized full article becomes available, review the fish sampling method, exact collection dates, taxa, effort, station-to-taxon results, and any voucher or specimen archive.
Until then, keep Estero Aviles as a historical source-named waterbody lead without adding fish species or treating the abstract's missing fish results as absence.
